topics.topic: Which canonical Workbench grammar revision governs an accepted review and whether later revisions affect it
questions: Which identifiable Workbench grammar revision governs this accepted review, and can a later grammar revision change whether the unchanged review passes?
Which Workbench grammar revision governs a review, and does a later grammar change revalidate or invalidate an already accepted review?
Which exact grammar and revision determine the required category set and record validity, and does an accepted review remain governed by that revision after the Workbench grammar changes?

quotes:
State 3 is blocked while the record fails the gate: when a referenced item is
removed from the index, or an APPLICABLE category is left without an accepted
decision of States 0–2 among its references.
judgement.why: The governing grammar revision is a State 2 gate decision, but the texts neither identify a revision nor establish that Workbench grammar revisions can change after acceptance, so no admissible upgrade witness can be built from them.
judgement.owner_question: Which identifiable Workbench security-review grammar revision governs A21, and can a later revision affect the unchanged accepted review automatically or only after explicit migration and renewed acceptance?
options: Freeze the grammar revision used when A21 is accepted.
Use the grammar supplied by the Workbench checkout that later runs design_lint.
Require an explicit migration and renewed acceptance before a newer grammar applies.
consequences: A later grammar change either leaves the accepted review valid, immediately changes whether it passes, or applies only after an explicit migration and renewed acceptance.
judgement.requirement_missing: no accepted requirement distinguishes the outcomes, or the product choice itself is missing; the author must establish the owner, not infer permitted freedom from silence

topics.topic: Whether category references may include non-decision items in addition to required accepted decisions
questions: Are the locally stated reference conditions exhaustive, or does the unnamed canonical grammar impose additional restrictions such as forbidding non-decision references alongside the required decision on an APPLICABLE category?

May a category's references include indexed items other than accepted decisions, provided an APPLICABLE category also references at least one accepted decision, or are such additional references forbidden?

quotes:
state2_security_gate_pass
<-> every_required_category_has_one_outcome
    AND every_reference_resolves_to_an_indexed_item
    AND every_APPLICABLE_references_an_accepted_decision_of_states_0_to_2
    AND no_UNRESOLVED

2. Every reference resolves to an indexed item, and every APPLICABLE category
   references at least one indexed accepted decision of States 0–2.
   [witness: workbench:state2_rules_decisions]
judgement.why: The biconditional and required test state an existential accepted-decision requirement alongside a separate resolution requirement for every reference, so additional resolved indexed items are not forbidden.
options: Any indexed item may be referenced, provided every reference resolves and an APPLICABLE category includes at least one accepted decision.
Restrict APPLICABLE references to accepted decisions only.
consequences: A mixed reference list passes when all entries resolve and at least one is an accepted decision; no decisions-only restriction is stated.

topics.topic: How design_lint should use the canonical Workbench grammar without creating a drifting duplicate
questions: How should the checking layer consume or reproduce the Workbench's canonical grammar without creating an independently drifting definition?

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
State 2: decide required results and constraints, including necessary refusal precedence; carry test mechanisms, exact contracts and deployment procedures to their owners.
